query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Grain refinement through hot rolling and subsequent annealing can improve the dynamic strength-ductility performance of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy alloy with a single body-centered cubic structure
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain size and increased grain boundary area
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and precipitation strengthening due to the formation of fine σ particles
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and ductility, with a potential increase in specific yield strength
generation.baseline: As-cast high-entropy alloy without hot rolling and annealing
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with a single body-centered cubic structure and processed through hot rolling and annealing
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of grain refinement and its effect on dynamic strength-ductility performance may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the dynamic strength-ductility performance of as-cast high-entropy alloys with and without hot rolling and annealing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hot-rolled and annealed alloy does not show improved yield strength and ductility compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Effect of Si on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of FeCrNi Medium Entropy Alloys

Abstract: FeCrNi medium entropy alloy (MEA) has been widely regarded for its excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance. However, insufficient strength limits its industrial application. Intermetallic particle dispersion strengthening is considered to be an effective method to improve strength, which is expected to solve this problem. In this work, microstructural evolution and mechanical behavior of FeCrNi MEA with different Si content were investigated. We found that the precipitation of fine σ particles can be formed in situ by thermomechanical treatment of Si doping FeCrNi MEAs. The FeCrNiSi0.15 MEA exhibits a good combination of strength and ductility, with yield strength and tensile elongation of 1050 MPa and 7.84%, respectively. The yield strength is almost five times that of the as-cast FeCrNi MEA. The strength enhancement is mainly attributed to the grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation strengthening caused by fine σ particles.

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
